# 11 Parse create/destroy participant statements and box groupings

## Outcome

`parseSequenceDiagram` recognizes `create participant X` / `create actor X` (a participant
declaration mid-statement-stream, `origin: "created"`) and `destroy X` (ends a previously declared
or created participant's lifeline at that point). It also recognizes
`box <color>? <label>? ... end` wrapping one or more `participant`/`actor` preamble declarations,
producing a `SequenceBox` referencing their ids.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `create participant Carl` / `create actor D as Donald` parse to a `participant` statement at
  that position in the stream, `origin: "created"`.
- [ ] `destroy Carl` parses to a `destroy` statement referencing `Carl`.
- [ ] `box Purple Alice,Bob \n participant Alice \n participant Bob \n end` parses to one
  `SequenceBox` with `label: "Purple"`-or-color-per-implementer's-chosen-parse (Mermaid's `box`
  header is `box <color-or-nothing> <label-or-nothing>` — document which token-order rule this
  ticket implements, since Mermaid's own grammar for this line is looser than a fixed field
  order) whose `participantIds` are `["Alice", "Bob"]`.
- [ ] `box transparent ... end` (explicit "no background") parses without error.
- [ ] A `destroy` referencing a participant id with no prior declaration is *not* rejected at
  parse time (ticket 12's job); parser only validates syntax shape.
- [ ] `create`/`destroy`/`box` interleave correctly with plain messages and control-flow blocks
  from tickets 01/06 — a `destroy` can appear inside a `loop` body, for example.

## Test seam

`parseSequenceDiagram(source: string): ParseResult` — unit level, pure function, extending ticket
06's test file.
